purpose: The Florentine Codex Book 4 augury pack in this directory holds seventy-two day-sign statements that cannot be applied to a birth because no civil-date correlation is approved. This manifest supplies the candidate correlations themselves, each with its anchor, its source and its evidence grade, so that the engine can apply one as a disclosed configured_method with the fork shown, rather than continuing to refuse for want of a candidate set.

candidates.label: Caso, fall-of-Tenochtitlan anchor
candidates.attributed_to: Alfonso Caso (1967, Los calendarios prehispanicos; 1971, Calendrical Systems of Central Mexico)
candidates.anchor_statement: 13 August 1521 in the Julian calendar is the day 1 Coatl, in the year 3 Calli.
candidates.notes: The field default. The anchoring event is the fall of Tenochtitlan, a date recorded in colonial sources in both counts.

candidates.label: Caso, Spanish-entry anchor
candidates.anchor_statement: 8 November 1519 in the Julian calendar is the day 8 Ehecatl, the ninth day of Quecholli, in the year 1 Acatl.
candidates.notes: Caso's second recorded anchor. It does not agree with the 1521 anchor; see the fork record.

candidates.label: Tena, 26 February year start
candidates.anchor_statement: The xiuhpohualli year begins on 26 February, on the day 1 Atlcahualo.
candidates.notes: The consulted survey reports the tonalpohualli count as displaced by seven days relative to Caso, and reports no secondary correction. Neither the displacement nor the year-start rule can be encoded as an anchor until Tena's own statement is obtained.

candidates.label: Nuttall-Ochoa, equinox-locked with intercalation
candidates.attributed_to: Zelia Nuttall, developed by Ruben Ochoa
candidates.anchor_statement: Caso's 1 Coatl date is retained, an intercalary correction is applied, and 1 Cipactli is placed exactly one day after the observable spring equinox.
candidates.notes: An observational rule, not a fixed day count: the anchor moves with the observed equinox, so it cannot be reduced to a single JDN offset. Recorded as a candidate family, not as an applicable profile.

candidates.label: Meza, fixed Cipactli year start
candidates.anchor_statement: The new year begins on the day Cipactli every year.
candidates.notes: A fixed Cipactli year start cannot hold across a 365-day year against a 260-day count, because 365 is not a multiple of 20. Recorded so the candidate set is complete and so the incompatibility is on the record.

candidates.label: Rodriguez Cortes, living Chiapas count
candidates.anchor_statement: No published anchor was located in this pass.
candidates.notes: A contemporary count carried by a living practitioner. It cannot be adopted from a webpage; it would require that practitioner's own participation and consent.

forks.statement: Caso's two anchors do not agree. Counting the 260-day cycle back from the 1521 anchor gives a different tonalpohualli day for 8 November 1519 than the day Caso records for it.
forks.independent_check: This repository recomputed the elapsed Julian day count and the 260-day positions from first principles and reproduced the discrepancy exactly: the 1521 anchor implies 7 Cipactli for 8 November 1519, while Caso records 8 Ehecatl. The offset is one day.
forks.sources_own_resolution: The consulted peer-reviewed restatement reports Caso's own resolution: that the Mexica day began at noon, so that one European calendar day can correspond to two adjacent tonalpohualli days depending on the time of the event.
forks.engine_policy: Both anchors are kept. A reading that applies one must name it, name the other, and state that the two differ by one day and why. Averaging them, or silently choosing one, is forbidden.

check_dates_available.description: Four Codex Borgia xiuhmolpilli dates are given in the same article in Julian reckoning and can be used to test any candidate that yields a day count.
check_dates_available.caveat: These are year-bearer plus day-sign pairs reported by a modern author from Caso's tables; they test consistency with Caso, not independence from him.
